Sanjeev AI: Deployment & Testing Strategy ​

To independently test features and safely deploy to production without breaking the live app, we need a deployment strategy that isolates environments and automates the testing process.

Given our current stack (React/Vite, Firebase, Google Cloud), the most powerful, seamless, and cost-effective framework is a combination of Firebase Environments, GitHub Actions, and Firebase Preview Channels.

1. Environment Isolation (The Foundation) ​

Instead of having one massive database where test data mixes with real user data, we create entirely separate Firebase Projects.

  • Local (The Sandbox): You use the Firebase Local Emulator Suite. This runs Firestore, Functions, and Auth entirely on your local machine so you can test code instantly without paying for cloud reads/writes.
  • Staging (sanjeev-ai-staging): A cloud project that exactly mirrors Production. This is where we test complex integrations (like YouTube OAuth and Vertex AI) before users see them.
  • Production (sanjeev-ai): The live app. Code only reaches here once it has survived Staging.

2. The Workflow (How it operates day-to-day) ​

We will adopt a simple branch-based workflow (often called GitHub Flow).

  1. Develop: You create a new feature branch (e.g., feature/youtube-shorts). You build it locally using the Emulators.
  2. Pull Request (PR): You push the branch to GitHub and open a Pull Request.
  3. Automated CI & Preview:
    • GitHub Actions automatically runs your linter and unit tests.
    • The Magic Trick: Firebase automatically generates a Preview URL (e.g., pr-12-sanjeev-ai.web.app). This gives you a live, isolated link to test your new feature before merging it.
  4. Merge to Staging: Once approved, the PR merges into the staging branch. GitHub Actions automatically deploys the frontend and backend functions to the Staging Firebase project.
  5. Promote to Prod: After final verification in Staging, you merge staging into main, which automatically deploys everything to the live users.

3. The Recommended Tooling Stack ​

CategoryRecommended ToolWhy it's the best choice for Sanjeev AI
CI/CD PipelineGitHub ActionsNative to GitHub, free for open/private repos, and officially supported by Firebase's deployment tools.
Unit & Component TestsVitestSince you are already using Vite for the frontend, Vitest is significantly faster and easier to configure than Jest.
End-to-End (E2E) TestsPlaywrightThe modern standard. It can open a real browser, click the "Generate" button, wait for the AI, and verify the video was created.
Backend TestingFirebase EmulatorsRun cloud functions and database triggers locally without deploying or waiting for cloud logs.

Current Implementation Status ​

We have successfully implemented the core CI/CD pipeline across our environments.

✅ Step 1: Firebase Environments (Completed) ​

We have linked the codebase (.firebaserc) to two isolated projects:

  • Staging: sanjeev-ai-staging
  • Production: sanjeev-ai
  • Development: gen-lang-client-0059629431

✅ Step 2: GitHub Branch Workflow (Completed) ​

We operate a strict multi-branch flow:

  • feature/* branches for local development.
  • staging branch for staging deployments.
  • main branch for production deployments.

✅ Step 3: GitHub Actions CI/CD (Completed) ​

We have fully automated our deployment pipeline using three dedicated workflows:

  1. firebase-hosting-pull-request.yml: Generates preview URLs against the staging project for any PR.
  2. firebase-hosting-merge-staging.yml: Deploys to sanjeev-ai-staging.web.app when merging to staging.
  3. firebase-hosting-merge-prod.yml: Deploys to sanjeev-ai.web.app when merging to main.

✅ Step 4: Environment Variables (Completed) ​

We have restructured our .env files to dynamically route API keys and Auth Domains:

  • .env.local for local emulators.
  • .env.staging for the staging environment (built via npm run build:staging).
  • .env.production for the production environment (built via npm run build).

Additionally, GitHub Actions securely injects Service Account JSON keys (FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_SANJEEV_AI_STAGING, FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_SANJEEV_AI) which are used by Playwright's global-setup.ts to mint Firebase Custom Tokens (e2e-test-user). This safely bypasses Google OAuth popups during CI/CD execution.

✅ Step 5: Frontend Testing (Completed) ​

  • Vitest is fully implemented for unit testing utility functions and React hooks.
  • Playwright is fully implemented for End-to-End UI testing, running against live backend environments using Custom Tokens.
  • The tsconfig.app.json has been hardened to securely exclude all *.test.ts, *.spec.ts, and e2e/ directories from the final Vite production build.

⏳ Pending Next Steps ​

  • Configure GitHub Branch Protection rules to mandate PR reviews before merging into staging or main.
